[[Caracas F.C.|Caracas]] were the defending champions. The competition was suspended on 12 March due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela|COVID-19 pandemic]], with all the results recorded until then voided on 15 May, and was reset starting from 14 October with a new format, ending on 15 December 2020. [[Deportivo La Guaira F.C.|Deportivo La Guaira]] won their first league title, beating [[Deportivo Táchira F.C.|Deportivo Táchira]] by a score of 2–0 in the final played at [[Valencia, Carabobo|Valencia]]. ==Format changes== ===Original format=== The league format changed for the 2020 season. No [[Apertura and Clausura]] tournaments would be held and the 20 teams would face each other in a home-and-away [[round-robin tournament]], for a total of 38 matches per team. The top eight teams of the first stage would advance to the semi-final stage, depending on eligibility requirements for CONMEBOL tournaments. The bottom two teams would be relegated. In the semi-final stage, the eight teams would be divided in two groups of four teams each, facing the other teams in their group twice. The two group winners would advance to the Serie Final to decide the league champions.{{cite web|url=https://www.laligafutve.com/read/temporada-2020-de-la-liga-futve-arrancara-el-26-de-enero|language=es|work=Liga FUTVE|date=8 January 2020|access-date=9 January 2020|title=Temporada 2020 de la Liga FUTVE arrancará el 26 de enero}}{{Dead link|date=January 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ===New format=== Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela|COVID-19 pandemic]], the league was suspended on 12 March.{{cite web |url=http://www.liderendeportes.com/noticias/football/suspendida-proxima-jornada-de-la-liga-futve/|title=Suspendida próxima jornada de la Liga Futve |publisher=Líder|language=es|date=12 March 2020}} On 15 May, the [[Venezuelan Football Federation|FVF]] announced the permanent suspension of the competition, with all first stage matches being voided.{{cite web |url=http://www.liderendeportes.com/noticias/slider/fvf-suspende-la-temporada-2020-de-la-liga-futve/|title=FVF suspende la temporada 2020 de la Liga FutVe|publisher=Líder|language=es|date=15 May 2020}} On 18 September, a new format was announced by the FVF and the Liga FUTVE, with the teams divided in two groups, playing each other twice. The group winners decided the league champions in a single match, and the next three teams of each group were awarded the remaining berths for CONMEBOL tournaments. Matches were played in [[Barinas, Barinas|Barinas]], [[Puerto Cabello]] and [[Valencia, Carabobo|Valencia]]. Relegation was suspended until 2021.{{cite web |url=https://www.balonazos.com/definieron-grupos-sedes-y-formato-del-torneo-2020-liga-futve-de-primera-division/|title=Definieron Grupos, Sedes y Formato del Torneo 2020 Liga FutVe de Primera División|publisher=Balonazos|language=es|date=18 September 2020|access-date=29 September 2020}} Due to the format change of the Copa Sudamericana, the play-offs to decide the order of berths for the tournament were not played. ==Teams== On 24 January, [[Llaneros Escuela de Fútbol|Llaneros]] was administratively relegated to the [[Venezuelan Segunda División|Segunda División]] by FVF as ordered by [[FIFA]] due to a lawsuit by former player [[Leonardo Ossa]], whom the club failed to pay an outstanding debt. Llaneros played in the second tier during the 2020 season,{{cite web|url=https://www.federacionvenezolanadefutbol.org/la-fvf-acato-decision-de-la-fifa-y-el-club-llaneros-ef-fue-descendido-a-segunda-division/|language=es|work=FVF|date=24 January 2020|title=La FVF acató decisión de la FIFA y el Club Llaneros EF fue descendido a segunda división}} therefore the league was contested by 19 teams. on 12 March the Liga FUTVE announced the suspension of the seventh round of matches, scheduled for the weekend of 14–15 March. That same day, the [[Venezuelan Football Federation|FVF]] announced the suspension of every footballing activity in the country. On 15 March, the Liga FUTVE cancelled a meeting originally scheduled for 18 March and also confirmed the indefinite suspension of the Primera División tournament.{{cite web|url=https://www.sportsvenezuela.com/liga-futve-fue-suspendida-de-forma-indefinida-por-el-covid-19/|title=Liga FUTVE fue suspendida de forma indefinida por el COVID-19|publisher=Sportsvenezuela.com|language=es|date=15 March 2020|access-date=16 March 2020|archive-date=23 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200323235416/https://www.sportsvenezuela.com/liga-futve-fue-suspendida-de-forma-indefinida-por-el-covid-19/|url-status=dead}} On 15 May, and after an emergency meeting held the previous day via video conference, the FVF announced the "permanent suspension" of the Primera and Segunda División seasons due to the inability to resume play under the conditions initially stated in the league regulations, effectively voiding the standings and results of matches played up until the suspension of the season. At the same time, the Federation's Commission of Club Competitions was tasked with elaborating a new tournament with a format and regulations suited to the necessary conditions for its execution, considering the application of sporting merit, club licensing requirements, and medical protocols. That same day, the Liga FUTVE issued a statement in which it rejected the suspension and voiding of the results of the 2020 season by the FVF, stating that the decision was made without consulting the league nor the teams, which was deemed to be as "a disrespect as well as putting at risk the economic and sports stability" of sports institutions.{{cite web |url=https://meridiano.net/futbol/futbol-venezolano/209620/liga-futve-rechaza-suspension-de-la-temporada-2020.html|title=Liga Futve rechaza suspensión de la temporada 2020|publisher=Meridiano|language=es|date=15 May 2020|access-date=9 September 2020}} In early June both the FVF and the Liga FUTVE presented, on their own, proposals to resume the competition. While the organization administering the league proposed to resume the tournament at the point at which it was suspended and play a single round-robin instead of a double round-robin as originally planned, with matches played only in the [[Carabobo|Carabobo state]], the governing body proposed to play a new tournament from scratch with the teams split into two groups according to geographical proximity.{{cite web |url=https://www.el-carabobeno.com/fvf-y-liga-futve-presentan-propuestas-con-estado-carabobo-como-protagonista/|title=FVF y Liga Futve presentan propuestas con estado Carabobo como protagonista|publisher=El Carabobeño|language=es|date=5 June 2020|access-date=9 September 2020}} On 14 June, the Venezuelan government authorized clubs to resume their training sessions starting from 15 June under biosecurity protocols and announced that the organizers of the football league had to put together a plan along with the National Institute of Sport (IND) to establish the new schedule and dates for the competition. Activities were also restricted to the "Carabobo-[[Yaracuy]] axis" as those were two of the states with the lowest rates of infection for COVID-19.{{cite web |url=https://www.laprensalara.com.ve/nota/17412/2020/06/autorizan-la-vuelta-a-la-actividad-del-futbol-venezolano|title=Autorizan la vuelta a la actividad del fútbol venezolano|publisher=La Prensa de Lara|language=es|date=15 June 2020|access-date=9 September 2020}} However, following a letter sent to the FVF by FIFA in which it confirmed that the power to organize the national football league rested in the national governing body, on 10 July the Liga FUTVE decided to withdraw their proposal to resume the competition, leaving the responsibility to organize the tournament on the FVF.{{cite web |url=http://www.balonazos.com/la-luga-futve-emite-comunicado-y-anuncia-retiro-de-propuesta-de-jugar-en-valencia/|title=Liga FutVe emite comunicado y anuncia retiro de propuesta de jugar en Valencia|publisher=Balonazos|language=es|date=10 July 2020|access-date=9 September 2020}} On 7 September, [[Zulia F.C.|Zulia]] announced that they would not be taking part in the tournament, arguing that the adequate biosecurity conditions were not in place to resume activities. That same day, [[LALA FC|LALA]] also declined to take part due to the same issues raised by Zulia. The new format was announced on 18 September, with the group stage taking place in [[Barinas, Barinas|Barinas]], [[Puerto Cabello]] and [[Valencia, Carabobo|Valencia]]. ==First stage== The first stage began on 30 January. Each team would play each other twice for 36 matchdays. It was scheduled to end on 25 October with the top eight teams advancing to the semi-finals and the bottom team being relegated.
